name: Ruth Farah
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember cutting my first tile across my knees.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Ruth by a small Friday habit. Ruth prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I built her an iron rest from a broken tile. She's finally willing to let me mend something in her house.
appearance: Ruth has short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat, a straight nose and deep-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a soft blue checked shirt. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Ruth steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Ruth admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Ruth learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To let the neighbor choose the next small household repair.
family: Verity Long is Ruth’s cousin raised in the same household. Ruth brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Verity makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The porch light*, Verity says, “I can afford the house only with a lodger. The owner asked if that meant strangers all the time.”
connections: Aubrey Farah. A house call to apologize becomes an opportunity to return the mended iron rest.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Ruth lets the child choose whether to stand by the door or sit beside the window while another adult gets help.
